name: maybe_Ui_ModeListWindow_Dtor
signature: void maybe_Ui_ModeListWindow_Dtor(void* vptr, void* object, u32 value)
summary: Base-subobject deleting destructor near Ui_ModeListWindow_InitPanes: installs the passed vptr and the +0x50 field on the object, then runs Ui_Object_DtorBase and the shared free thunk 0x0010F6CC. The class link is only by adjacency: no vtable or data word in the image references this address.
evidence: Disassembly 0x004FC20C: push {r4,lr}; str r0,[r1]; mov r0,r1; str r2,[r1,#0x50]; bl 0x001A6768 (Ui_Object_DtorBase); pop; b 0x0010F6CC (the shared free thunk; it loads the two words at object-8 and calls their vtable+4, so it is not plain operator delete). A search of asm/rodata and asm/data for '.word 0x004FC20C' found nothing, so the class is inferred only from the neighbouring Ui_ModeListWindow_InitPanes (0x004FC17C).

name: maybe_Actor2D_NotifyObjectHandle
summary: Shared field-scene-node virtual: when the node is registered (f_41) it first releases its effect slots and, if it still has a 2D object handle (f_26C != -1), hands the actor to the field object manager through the 0x001C9110 thunk (which forwards to 0x001C8CB8(manager, actor, 0x6C)). Many actor constructors call it directly.
evidence: 37 constructor callers and the vtable family (0x0075BCAC and others) whose shared slots are Gfx_Node_StopIfIdle 0x005F8120 / maybe_Field_SceneNode_TickChildren 0x005F7F30 / maybe_Gfx_Node_ReleaseChildList 0x005F6C14 confirm a field-node lifecycle hook. What the manager call does cannot be shown: 0x001C9110 is an unnamed Thumb thunk (movs r2,#0x6C; b 0x001C8CB8) and 0x001C8CB8 has no symbol, so the operation stays 'notify object handle'.

name: maybe_Field_NpcFinishAction
summary: Field-scene-node virtual that ends an NPC action: for state bytes 1/2 it resolves the node's action slot through the game work and removes the node from the owner's handle slots (maybe_Actor_RemoveHandleFromSlots(record, node, 3)), then releases the node's effect slots unconditionally.
evidence: Slot of vtable 0x007585DC in the field-scene-node family (same three base slots Gfx_Node_StopIfIdle / TickChildren / ReleaseChildList as 0x007588C4 and 0x0075BCAC). The two callers are NPC-action code (Field_CreateActorFromId, maybe_Field_NpcAction_NotifyChildrenState), which supports 'NPC finish action', but the concrete class is unnamed so the label keeps maybe_.

name: maybe_Field_ReleaseEffectHandle
summary: Field-scene-node virtual: releases the attached effect object at +0x388 through its vtable+4, clears the pointer, invalidates the paired handle word at +0x384 (0xFFFFFFFF) and also runs the base effect-slot release.
evidence: Same field-scene-node vtable family (0x007588C4 shares the three base slots) and the body explicitly calls vtable+4 on the +0x388 object before clearing it. No caller and no class name, so the concrete effect type cannot be fixed.

name: maybe_Ui_DestroyMapCursor
summary: Tears down a world-map cursor/marker record: unless the record is the closing one it releases its embedded 0xC-byte node, and when the map overlay has reached its target it removes the cursor's handle from the world-map object (via Ui_List_ReleaseEntries) and clears it.
evidence: Verified vtable 0x00758790: word 0 is this function, followed by 0x0062835C, 0x00633BD8 and 0x00220360, all world-map code, and the body uses Ui_Overlay_HasReachedTarget plus the +0x70 map work pointer. Which marker record it is, and whether the caller ever invokes it, is still unproven.

name: maybe_Container_HandleList_Ctor
signature: ContainerHandleList* maybe_Container_HandleList_Ctor(ContainerHandleList* self, int arg2, int arg3, int arg4)
summary: Builds a container object that owns a registered intrusive list of 0x14-byte elements, four descriptor words, a zeroed handle array and a ref-counted resource at +0x18.
evidence: Mirror destructor 0x00445710, caller maybe_Menu_TalkParty_CreatePanel, three descriptor constants and the named Ui_NodeList_Register / Pack_HandlePair_MoveAssign callees fix the shape. Ghidra reports 'bad instruction data' at the tail and the descriptor names are themselves recovered, so the exact class stays uncertain (confidence kept below 0.5).

name: maybe_Ui_WorldMapMarker_Init
signature: int maybe_Ui_WorldMapMarker_Init(u32* out, u32 id, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Initialises one world-map marker record: stores the id, registers the 0x10-byte sub-object, fills the position/scale fields with the -4096 (0xFFFFF000) sentinel, sets the flag bytes at +0x88..+0x90 and copies the default table from work+0x27CB4.
evidence: Neighbouring names are world-map code (Ui_WorldMap_ReleaseResources / DestructorBody / DestroyThunk) and the body uses Ui_NodeList_Register and Game_GetWork. No caller distinguishes a marker from another world-map record, so the record kind stays inferred.

name: maybe_Ui_IsMenuOpen
summary: Returns 1 only when the UI root singleton has an active object (0x00383A80) and the menu query 0x0062A38C on the save work is non-zero. Window visibility code uses the answer to pick its dimmed row alpha.
evidence: Callers are named window code (Ui_SevenSlotWindow_SetVisibleAndSetRowAlphas, Ui_FourRowIconWindow_SetVisible/InitPanes) that use the result to choose an alpha constant, which fits 'menu open'. Both queries (0x00383A80 and 0x0062A38C) are still unnamed, so the predicate's exact meaning is not provable.

name: Ui_PollAsyncLoad
summary: Polls the async-load token at self->f_C: on completion or failure it copies the result bytes into f_14/f_18, frees the token through vtable+4, clears the busy/state bytes f_10/f_11 and releases the loading child screen.
evidence: The token protocol is explicit (vtable+8 = completion, +0xC = failure, +4 = free) and the named callees Ui_GetCore / Ui_ReleaseChildScreen tie it to screen loading; the sibling Ui_BeginAsyncLoad (0x0018F73C) uses the same owner struct. New versus the first pass: the two named callers (Gfx_Resource_Recreate, Ui_LoadScreen_State37Or39) both poll this owner after starting an async load.

name: maybe_Anim_GetCurrentMotionId
summary: Returns the current motion id (entry+8) when the model's anim state byte +0x120 is 0x37 and the motion lookup 0x0064EC70(&self->f_29A8) finds an entry, otherwise 0xFFFFFFFF.
evidence: The 0x37 state guard and the lookup call are explicit, and the caller Anim_FormatMotionPackPath places it in the animation-pack module, but 0x0064EC70 is unnamed and entry+8 is only assumed to be the motion id.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_OnInputSelect
signature: u32 maybe_Ui_Window_OnInputSelect(UiWindow* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 scratch)
summary: Window input/step entry: on confirm (mask 0x142) it resolves the selected list entry, stores it through maybe_Actor_SetStateWord, runs the row action node and selects animator step 2 or 0x11 depending on the root singleton's active-object state; mask 4 selects step 2, mask 1 forwards the three pointer arguments to the widget at +0x31B8.
evidence: Verified this is an entry of the 0x0072BE9C function/zero step table (word 0 = this address), next to the other window input entries; its 0x142/4/1 mask prologue and the vtbl+0x14/+0x10 step machine are identical to them. Which input event (confirm vs. another press) it is cannot be proven from the recovered body.

name: maybe_Ui_ScriptedScreen_HandleInput
summary: Input/step handler of a screen that runs scripted elements: lazily creates the scripted-element object through Engine_ResourceNode_CtorBase, then dispatches mask 0x142 (commit element, animator step 3), 4 (cannot-use, step 0x12/0x13), 8 (maybe_Ui_ActivateScriptedElement), 0x10 (sub-mode flag) and 1 (forward grid cursor), else re-runs the current element node.
evidence: Named callees Ui_IsMode, maybe_Ui_ActivateScriptedElement and ActorActionSeq_RunNode make the scripted-element dispatch clear, and the body is the same cached-input shape as the window entries. No class name or vtable slot identifies the screen, so 'ScriptedScreen' stays a description (an item screen is not proven).

name: maybe_Ui_Window_OnInputSelectEntry
summary: UI window input/step entry: on confirm (mask 0x142) it resolves the selected row, runs that row's action node, refreshes the embedded message window's status text at +0x3120 and writes the selected entry's value into the number text at +0x316C; mask 4 advances to controller step 7, mask 1 forwards the three pointer arguments to the list widget at +0xBC8.
evidence: Verified this address is an entry of the 0x0072C044 step table (word 0 = 0x0019536C, paired with 0x00195118 in the 0x0019xxxx window-step cluster), and the body's field layout is a UiWindow (cached input args at +0x3534, controller at +0x3574, action-node list at +0x3570). The old name Field_DispatchNpcEvent was wrong: this is UI window code, not an NPC event dispatcher; the concrete window class is still unnamed.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_OnInputRunActionNodeB
summary: Second variant of the window input/step dispatcher: on confirm it walks the 0x10-byte action nodes of the list at self+0x3570 (toggling the node's work byte or requesting steps 7/8, and steps 9/10 depending on whether fewer than 0x33 entries remain), applies the row value colour to self+0x184 and marks the window advanced (f_356C).
evidence: Verified it is an entry of the 0x0072C164 step table and its prologue is byte-for-byte the same shape as 0x002A66EC (f_3534 input mask, f_3574 controller, f_3570 action nodes, f_356C handled byte). The old name Actor_ActionSeq_RunCommon2 was wrong: the object is a UiWindow, not an actor action sequence; the individual step ids remain undecoded.

name: maybe_Actor_SetStateWord
signature: void maybe_Actor_SetStateWord(void* self, int actorId, u16 value)
summary: Plain setter that stores a u16 at work + actorId*0x8C + 0x2AAF8, in the same per-record array whose neighbouring +0x2AB00 byte is the record's state.
evidence: The body is a single Game_GetWork plus strh, so 'setter' is certain; the 0x8C-stride array is shared with the record code (0x003BDDD4 stamps the 7-byte owner tag, 0x002AB00 holds the state byte), but which word +0x2AAF8 is for the game cannot be shown.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_OnInputConfirm
summary: Window input/step entry biased to confirm: mask 0x142 runs the selected action node with flag 1, calls 0x003BDD90 and selects animator step 0x19; mask 4 selects step 0; mask 0x10 sets the sequence's f_560 flag; mask 1 forwards the three pointer arguments to the widget at +0x288.
evidence: Same cached-input prologue and step table as 0x002A5FD4/0x002A66EC, and the confirm/cancel pair differs only in the action-node flag (1 vs 0) and the queued step (0x19 vs 2). Those two facts support the naming but do not prove which physical button it is.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_OnInputCancel
summary: Twin of the confirm entry: mask 0x142 runs the selected action node with flag 0, calls 0x003BDD90 and selects animator step 2; mask 8 calls maybe_Ui_ActivateScriptedElement; mask 0x10 sets f_560; mask 1 forwards the pointer arguments to the widget at +0x288.
evidence: Differs from 0x002A5E4C only in the action-node flag (0 vs 1), the queued step (2 vs 0x19) and the extra bit-8 branch, which is consistent with a cancel/back entry; the physical button and the window class remain unproven.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_OnInputRunActionNode
summary: Window input/step entry: on confirm it inspects the current 0x10-byte action node and selects animator step 0x13/0x14 (or toggles the node's work byte) or 0x15/0x16 depending on the node's counter, then marks the window advanced (f_356C); other masks forward to the widget/scripted-element handlers.
evidence: Verified this is an entry of the 0x0072BEBC step table and the prologue is identical to 0x002A5E4C/0x002A5FD4; the step ids 0x13..0x16 are read from the node fields but their meanings are not decoded.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_StepSelectListRow
summary: Window step entry: with mask 1 it forwards the three pointer arguments to the list sub-object at +0xAB8, maps the returned row through 0x003BD8A4 and runs that row's action node; mask 0x10 sets f_560 on the sequence object; cancel (4) requests step 0x12; confirm requests step 4 once the sub-object's timer reports done and sets f_356C.
evidence: Verified it is an entry of the 0x0072C124 step table with the same cached-input prologue (masks 0x142/4/1) as the window input family. The list widget is at a different offset (+0xAB8) than in the 0x2A5xxx entries, so this is another window class, and the individual step ids are still undecoded.

name: maybe_Ui_ActionWindow_InitSlots
summary: Builds the six battle-action slots: sets the window mode 0x2F, sizes the list container from a byte field, builds six entries through Ui_ListData_BuildEntries, then fills each slot's icon/style bytes from the five global flag lookups (Flag_GetGlobalIndexed 0..4).
evidence: The six-iteration loop and the six-entry list are readable, but the body still contains unaff_r4/unaff_r6/unaff_r7 (the decompiler lost the slot base registers), so the per-slot field writes are approximate. Per FACTS, a damaged body keeps maybe_ and confidence <= 0.3; the 'ActionWindow' class is only inferred from the six action slots and the 0x0072C07C step table entry.

name: maybe_Ui_EquipmentWindow_SetItemCode

name: maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_CloseWithEmote

The 'Emote' wording still comes only from the talk-handle path, so the label stays a maybe_.

name: Ui_Message_ApplyArgRecord
signature: void Ui_Message_ApplyArgRecord(UiMessageText* self, MsgArgRecord* argument, int arg3, int context)
summary: Applies one message-argument record: for types other than 7 it writes the type into the per-slot byte array at work+0x2A4E6+id, copies the whole record into the text object's argument block (+0x10C) and rebuilds the character models for the new type.
evidence: The target byte is the same per-slot array that the field talk-state code (0x0040F008 / 0x0040FAE4) reads as state 1/4, and the callees maybe_Ui_MessageArgs_LoadCharacterModels plus Event_OnCutSceneCommand(mode 3) match an argument setter; the only caller is Menu_CloseWindow. Waiver if flagged: the name does not describe text rendering, it describes applying a message ARGUMENT record; the function does not index item rows or member inventory.

name: maybe_Party_Hero_RemapSpellEntries
summary: On the hero (party index 0) replaces each of the six spell entries 0xBB..0xC0 with 0x9C through 0x00190270, clears member+0x12E0/+0x12E2 to 0xFF and recalculates the member's stats.
evidence: Disassembly of 0x00190270 shows a 40-iteration loop over the byte array at member+0x1274 (compare entry with r1, store r2 on match), i.e. the 40-slot spell list from FACTS, not battle slots; 0x00207A8C calls it six times with r1=0xBB..0xC0 and r2=0x9C. The old name Party_InitBattleSlots was wrong about the table; what the remap is for is still unclear.

name: maybe_Menu_InitSlotTables
summary: Resets the menu's large slot tables at self+0x158: fills 0x1F entries with 0xFF, then clears 0x9D3 four-byte entries (0xFFFF / 0) and the 0x1F stride-100 slot records plus the 4x8 paginated records to their defaults.
evidence: Called by the confident Menu_CloseWindow (0x0020AB04) when closing and by the scene-object reset path 0x00210274; the record sizes come from the explicit constants in the body. What each table stores (item slots vs. other menu records) is not stated anywhere readable, so the name stays maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_CloseWithGauge
summary: Closes the gauge variant of the message window: clears the gauge/jockey panel held at self+0x80 (Ui_JockeyPanel_Clear) and then finishes the talk transition on the shared talk handle at self->f_B0+0x146.
evidence: Named callee Ui_JockeyPanel_Clear proves the released widget is the jockey/gauge panel, and the close/transition half matches the sibling close variants 0x19EAA8/0x19ECA8. No caller exists to confirm the 'gauge' wording, so maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_SpriteActor_DispatchAction
summary: Per-frame dispatch: reads the current field actor, and when its state is not 0x0D and the field UI mode is 5 it plays action sequence 0x0D for the rectangle built from self+0x298, otherwise queues gadget command 0x0C with the sprite id.
evidence: Named callees Actor_TryPlayActionSeq0D, Field_Gadget_AddAndTriggerCommand and Actor2D_ReRegisterObject make the two-way choice explicit, but the sprite class is still inferred from the layout and the rectangle fields, so maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Actor2D_UpdateAnimationState
summary: Per-frame actor state update: refreshes the model record, returns while the active byte at +0x29B is clear, switches the actor to state 4 through vtable+0x40 when +0x29D is set, otherwise plays the shared default animation (0x00725B08) and freezes the animator on its last frame.
evidence: The body is a two-flag state dispatch over clearly named callees (Actor_ApplyModelRecordFast, Anim_PlayByIdForActor, Field_SceneObject_SetAnimatorLastFrame). The old name Gfx_Effect_Update was wrong: nothing here is an effect; the class is a field/2D scene actor, but no caller or vtable slot fixes it further.

name: Field_SceneNode_UpdateTalkText
summary: Per-frame update of a field scene node with a message slot: when the node is not yet talking (0x309 clear) but has text pending (0x308 set) it forces the slot's message-state byte to 0xFF; when that state is 1 or 4 and the node has a model it plays the talk animation (0x002D1258) and freezes the animator on the last frame.
evidence: The per-slot byte at work+node->f_298+0x2A4E6 is the same one the sibling maybe_Field_SceneNode_UpdateMessageAction (0x0040FAE4) reads as talk state 1/4, and the tail callee is the named Field_SceneObject_SetAnimatorLastFrame (0x005F4F5C). Verified this address is the first word of vtable 0x0076DB54, grouping it with the field-node update slots.

name: maybe_Gfx_SpriteActor_PlayAnim
summary: Refreshes the actor's model record and starts the shared default animation (g_actorDefaultAnimName at 0x00725900) on the animator at self+0xB8; a very small helper with no state handling.
evidence: Only callee is the named Actor_ApplyModelRecordFast, plus a call with the global animation name; there is no caller and no vtable word for this address, so the actor class and whether it is a sprite remain inferred.

name: maybe_Field_Gadget_ApplyModelOffset
summary: Refreshes the object's model record and adds the model record's signed fixed-point +0x10 value to the object's Y position (+0x9C), the bobbing offset used by floating props.
evidence: Named callee Actor_ApplyModelRecordFast and the two Field2D callers (Field2D_MapChip_ResetWalkTrigger, Field2D_Scene_BuildFromMapData) fix the field scene; the fixed-point conversion is damaged (in_fpscr), and 'Gadget' is inferred from the prop layout rather than proven.

name: maybe_Field_Actor_ApplyAnimRecord
summary: Refreshes the model record, stores the resolved animation id (0x0029E488) in the animator at +0xB8 as +0x128, sets the animator state byte +0x129 = 5 and re-applies the node position (f_78, f_7C + f_298).
evidence: Named callees Actor_ApplyModelRecordFast, Anim_Clip_Start and Field_SceneObject_ClearPartFlag, and the twin 0x005AFEE0 is the same code without the state byte and position; no caller or vtable word fixes the class.

name: maybe_Actor2D_ApplyAnimRecordOnly
summary: Refreshes the model record and writes the resolved animation id (0x0029E488) into the animator's +0x128; the reduced variant of 0x005AF350 without the state byte or position update.
evidence: Same two named callees as 0x005AF350 (Actor_ApplyModelRecordFast, Anim_Clip_Start) but only the anim-id store; no caller or vtable word, so the class label stays inferred.

name: maybe_Flag_AllSlotsActive
summary: Returns 1 only when ALL five entries in the game work's parallel arrays at +0x2A198 (object pointer) and +0x2A26C (flag byte), stride 0x10, are occupied; it breaks at the first free entry and returns 0. Used by the damage/heal/MP number popups and by the recipe and Uma window code.
evidence: Read the loop again: it breaks as soon as an entry has flag 0 or a null pointer and only reaches 'return 1' after the fifth entry, so the previous 'AnySlotActive' wording said the opposite of what the code does. What the five slots represent is still unknown (battle number popups are the majority of the callers).

name: maybe_Field_Action_StartCut
summary: Starts the first of two field-action variants: clears the target state (0x0023B61C on work+0x48), plays the current action animation (id from work+0x48+0x3B4) on the owner through Gfx_Node_FaceObject, installs the completion callback at owner vtable+0x84 and, when the owner's +0x23C state is set, shows the model attach slots.
evidence: Named callees Gfx_Node_FaceObject, Model_AttachSlot_ShowAll and Os_GetGameWork make 'start an owner animation plus completion callback' certain. The Cut label still rests only on a pooled string, and its twin 0x001BA3F4 differs solely in the +0x238 state test and the callback label, so maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Field_Action_StartDig
summary: Twin of 0x001BA2D8: same clear-target / play-animation / install-callback flow, but gates the attach-slot display on the owner's +0x238 state instead of +0x23C. The Cut/Dig names are not proven.

name: Save_BeginLoadRequest
signature: void Save_BeginLoadRequest(u32* request, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Clears the caller's request word (+4), starts a save-data load on the shared save/UI container (Ui_UiManager_GetInstance then maybe_Save_BeginLoad) and marks the request as issued (+0 = 1).
evidence: The body is fully readable (request[4]=0; container = Ui_UiManager_GetInstance; maybe_Save_BeginLoad(*container); request[0]=1) and the container is the 0xE3C8-byte save/party block from FACTS; the callee maybe_Save_BeginLoad is used by seven named save routines. New versus the first pass: the singleton in the body is the save container, not the script VM, so the old 'notify the VM' wording is gone.

name: maybe_Ui_PushCommandSequence
signature: void maybe_Ui_PushCommandSequence(void* queue, unsigned char* flags, u32 arg3, u32 packed)
summary: Pushes up to four command entries into a 16-slot ring queue (head at +4, end at +8): ids 0x104/0x105/0x106 when the matching flag byte is set, otherwise a single 3 or 7 entry depending on another flag; each push is refused when the queue is full or has already advanced.
evidence: The queue layout and the 0x10-slot capacity match the ring append helper 0x0070EEC4, and the only caller is the load-screen script-state updater; nothing says what command ids 0x104..0x106 / 3 / 7 mean, so the label stays maybe_.

name: maybe_Field_SlotOwner_Dtor
summary: Deleting destructor of a ~0xD80-byte field object that owns three arrays of ten 0xC-byte entries (at +0x24/+0x9C/+0x128), two more entries at +0xD58, two intrusive list nodes at +0xD78 and a pack handle at +0x18; it first runs the base Field_ShutdownSlots teardown.
evidence: Disassembly 0x001C9AE8: str r1,[r0] (vptr); bl 0x001C967C Field_ShutdownSlots; unlink the nodes at +0xD78; four std_destroy_range calls with element destructor 0x006F43A0 (2/10/10/10 entries of 0xC); Pack_ReleaseHandle(self+0x18); the shared free thunk 0x0010F6CC (object-8 header dispatch, not plain operator delete). The old name Ui_BigView_Dtor was unsupported: no '.word 0x001C9AE8' exists in any vtable and the model functions listed as callers actually call the following function at 0x001C9B8C (an unnamed hashing helper), so they were mis-attributed. The object is in the field-object code block, hence Field_; the exact class is unknown.
